result:
Compiled successfully. I wrote `tests/org/apache/commons/csv/CSVPrinterAgentTest.java` (JUnit 3.8 style, `extends TestCase`) covering:

- Constructor contract: `IllegalArgumentException` for null `out`, null `format`, and inconsistent hybrid encapsulation/escaping formats; `getOut()` identity.
- `print`: plain values unquoted, delimiter insertion between fields, encapsulation when a value contains the delimiter or the quote char (with doubling), new-line reset of the leading-delimiter state.
- `println`: exact record-separator output for both `"\n"` and `"\r\n"`.
- `printComment`: no-op when comments are disabled (the documented default), correct `"# "` prefixing on a fresh line, forcing a new line when mid-record, and prefixing every line of a multi-line comment.
- `printRecord` (varargs and `Iterable`): delimiter-joined output terminated by the record separator, zero-value records, embedded-newline escaping, and successive calls producing successive lines.
- `printRecords` (`Iterable`, `Object[]`, and `ResultSet` via a `java.lang.reflect.Proxy`-based stub): one line per record/row, empty-input cases, and `SQLException` propagation from a failing `ResultSet`.
- `flush`: delegation to the underlying `Flushable`.
- `close`: doesn't throw and leaves prior output intact.

Only documented behavior (from `api/org/apache/commons/csv/CSVPrinter.html` and the package description) was asserted; I avoided guessing at undocumented details like null-value rendering or a `close()`→underlying-stream-close contract. `./compile.sh` reports `compiled OK`.
